1516905.title: VPN bound to VLAN interface as secondary IPsec gateway with two IPsec gateways
1516905.description:
Original ID: 21
Original Title: VPN bound to VLAN interface as secondary IPsec gateway with two IPsec gateways
Original Description: This test verifies that if a Primary IPSec Gateway is not reachable, secondary gateway is used to establish a tunnel, the tunnel can be establised.
1516905.result: The initial tunnel is established using the primaty gateway. After the cable on the primary WAN of SonicWALL2 has been disconnected, the ping from PC1 gets dropped. SonicWALL1 sends a configured number of DPD requests before the existing tunnel gets deleted. A new IKE_SA_INIT negotiation is initiated by ping. It uses the primary IPSec gateway first. This negotiation fails after 5 retries. A new IKE_SA_INIT negotiation starts and uses the secondary IPSec Gateway address(X2:v101). The new tunnel is established.

1516909.steps: 1) Configure Remote Gateway. Using X1 IP address of FW1 as the Primary ipsec gateway, Add a VPN policy on the firewall. choose main mode or aggressive mode Select the Local network obtains IP addresses using DHCP through this VPN Tunnel radio button under Local Networks. Select the Choose destination network from list option and select the address object Central Net (LAN subnet on the Central site) under Destination Networks. 2) Open DHCP over VPN Configuration window on the VPN > DHCP over VPN page on the Remote Gateway and set parameters. Enter Relay IP address and Management IP address. Those addresses must belong to the scope of LAN addresses of the Central Gateway. 3) Configure Central Gateway. Using X1:v101 IP address of FW2 as the Primary ipsec gateway, Add a VPN policy on the firewall. choose main mode or aggressive mode Select the Choose destination network from list option and select the address object LAN Primary Subnet under Local Networks. Select the Destination network obtains IP addresses using DHCP through this VPN Tunnel radio button under Destination Networks. 4) Configure the external DHCP server on the LAN of Central Gateway. Set the pool of addresses available for leasing. 5) Change the network configuration properties on the PC connected to the LAN of Remote Gateway to obtain IP address automatically (dhcp mode). 6) Send pings from the PC (DHCP Client) to a host on the LAN of Central Gateway.
1516909.initial: pc1-------(X0)FW1(x1)------(X1:v101)FW2(X0)-------pc2 FW1 is central firewall,FW2 is remote firewall
1516909.title: VPN bound to VLAN interface applied in DHCP relay topology
1516909.description:
Original ID: 26
Original Title: VPN bound to VLAN interface applied in DHCP relay topology
Original Description: This test case is to verify VPN bound to vlan interface can work in the DHCP relay topology.
1516909.result: 1.Remote Gateway is set automatically on the VPN > DHCP over VPN page when the Local network obtains IP addresses using DHCP through this VPN Tunnel radio button under Local Networks is selected in the VPN policy on Remote Gateway. 2.Current DHCP over VPN Leases table on Remote Gateway shows Relay IP and Management IP static entries. 3.The access rules for LAN to VPN and VPN to LAN on Remote Gateway show Vpn DHCP Clients and Central Net address objects. 4.The access rules for LAN to VPN and VPN to LAN on Central Gateway show LAN Primary Subnet and Vpn DHCP Clients address objects. 5.When the network configuration properties on the PC on the Remote site changed to dhcp mode, IKE negotiation is initiated by Remote Gateway and DHCP broadcast packets are passed through the tunnel. Ipconfig command returns the IP address obtained from the external DHCP server on the Central site. 6.Current DHCP over VPN Leases table on Remote Gateway is populated with a new entry. It shows IP address, computer name, and Ethernet address of the DHCP Client. The table is sent to Central Gateway upon negotiation. 7.Pings from the DHCP client to the host on Central network are returned.

1516908.steps: 1) Configure a VPN policy on the remote firewall using IKE Main mode. Using X1 IP address of FW1 as the Primary ipsec gateway, Select LAN Primary subnet object from a drop-down menu under Local Networks. Select Use this VPN Tunnel as default route for all Internet traffic radio button under Destination Networks. 2) Configure a VPN policy on the central firewall using IKE Main mode. Using X1:v101 IP address of FW2 as the Primary ipsec gateway, Select Any address under Local Networks. Select Rem network object from a drop-down menu under Destination Networks (the object previously added in the Network>Address Objects page). Don't specify Default LAN Gateway in the VPN policy. 3) Add a new policy in the Network>NAT Policies page on the central firewall. Set the fields: Source Original Rem network object, Source Translated central firewall's WAN IP address, Destination Original Any, Destination Translated Original, Service Original Any, Service Translated Original, Interface Inbound Any, Interface Outbound Any. 4) Send a ping to yahoo.com from a host behind the remote firewall.
1516908.initial: pc1-------(X0)FW1(x1)------(X1:v101)FW2(X0)-------pc2 FW1 is central firewall,FW2 is peer firewall

1516908.description:
Original ID: 25
Original Title: VPN bound to VLAN interface applied in Tunnel All topology
Original Description: This test case is to verify VPN bound to vlan interface can work fine in Tunnel All topology.
1516908.result: The ping to yahoo initiates IKE negotiation on the remote firewall. Pings are replied. The SA in IKE Main mode is negotiated successfully. The remote firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN>Settings page with its LAN subnet under Local and 0.0.0.0 ? 255.255.255.255 under Remote subnet. The central firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN>Settings page with 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255 under Local and the remote firewall's LAN subnet under Remote. The appropriate log messages are generated on the both firewalls. Packet Trace on the Diagnostics page shows ESP packets exchange while pings to yahoo are sent from the remote site.
